items.informal_name: Cardinality of Filtered Dependent Product via Snoc Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {n : ℕ} {α : Fin (n + 1) → Type u_1} (S : (i : Fin (n + 1)) → Finset (α i)) (P : ((i : Fin n) → α i.castSucc) → Prop)
  [inst : DecidablePred P],
  {r ∈ Fintype.piFinset S | P (Fin.init r)}.card =
    (S (Fin.last n)).card * {r ∈ Fintype.piFinset (Fin.init S) | P r}.card
items.informal_description: The cardinality of the set of functions $ r $ in the dependent product $ \prod_{i} S(i) $ satisfying predicate $ P $ on the initial segment $ \mathrm{init}(r) $ equals the product of the cardinality of the last component $ S(\mathrm{last}) $ and the cardinality of the set of functions in $ \prod_{i < \mathrm{last}} S(i) $ satisfying $ P $. Formally, $ |\{ r \in \prod S \mid P(\mathrm{init}(r)) \}| = |S(\mathrm{last})| \cdot |\{ r \in \prod_{i < \mathrm{last}} S(i) \mid P(r) \}| $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Filtered Dependent Product with Tail Predicate
items.type:
∀ {n : ℕ} {α : Fin (n + 1) → Type u_1} (S : (i : Fin (n + 1)) → Finset (α i)) (P : ((i : Fin n) → α i.succ) → Prop)
  [inst : DecidablePred P],
  {r ∈ Fintype.piFinset S | P (Fin.tail r)}.card = (S 0).card * {r ∈ Fintype.piFinset (Fin.tail S) | P r}.card
items.informal_description: The cardinality of the set of functions $ r $ in the product of $ S $ over $ \mathrm{Fin}(n+1) $ satisfying predicate $ P $ applied to $ \mathrm{tail}\, r $ equals the product of the cardinality of $ S(0) $ and the cardinality of the set of functions $ r' $ in the product of $ S $ over $ \mathrm{Fin}(n) $ satisfying $ P(r') $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Filtered Cartesian Product by Predicate Agreement
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (s : Finset α) (t : Finset β) (p : α → Prop) (q : β → Prop) [inst : DecidablePred p]
  [inst_1 : DecidablePred q],
  {x ∈ s ×ˢ t | p x.1 = q x.2}.card =
    (Finset.filter p s).card * (Finset.filter q t).card + {x ∈ s | ¬p x}.card * {x ∈ t | ¬q x}.card
items.informal_description: Given finite sets $ S $ and $ T $, and predicates $ P : S \to \{\text{true}, \text{false}\} $ and $ Q : T \to \{\text{true}, \text{false}\} $, the cardinality of the subset of $ S \times T $ consisting of pairs $ (a, b) $ where $ P(a) = Q(b) $ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of the $ P $-filtered $ S $ and $ Q $-filtered $ T $, plus the product of the cardinalities of the complements of these filtered sets. Formally, $ |\{(a, b) \in S \times T \mid P(a) = Q(b)\}| = |\{a \in S \mid P(a)\}| \cdot |\{b \in T \mid Q(b)\}| + |\{a \in S \mid \neg P(a)\}| \cdot |\{b \in T \mid \neg Q(b)\}| $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Filtered Product Set After Index Removal
items.type:
∀ {n : ℕ} {α : Fin (n + 1) → Type u_1} {p : Fin (n + 1)} (S : (i : Fin (n + 1)) → Finset (α i))
  (P : ((i : Fin n) → α (p.succAbove i)) → Prop) [inst : DecidablePred P],
  {r ∈ Fintype.piFinset S | P (p.removeNth r)}.card = (S p).card * {r ∈ Fintype.piFinset (p.removeNth S) | P r}.card
items.informal_description: For a finite type $\alpha = \mathrm{Fin}(n+1)$, a family of finite sets $S : \alpha \to \mathrm{Finset}$, and a decidable predicate $P$ on functions $\mathrm{Fin}(n) \to \bigcup_{i} S_i$, the cardinality of the set $\{ r \in \prod_{i \in \alpha} S_i \mid P(r^{(p)}) \}$ equals $|S_p| \times |\{ r' \in \prod_{i \neq p} S_i \mid P(r') \}|$, where $r^{(p)}$ denotes the function with the $p$-th index removed.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Filtered Dependent Product Set with Fixed Index Value
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_4} {α : ι → Type u_6} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)]
  (s : (i : ι) → Finset (α i)) (i : ι) (a : α i),
  {f ∈ Fintype.piFinset s | f i = a}.card = if a ∈ s i then ∏ b ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, (s b).card else 0
items.informal_description: For a finite index type $\iota$ and a family of finite sets $s(i)$ indexed by $\iota$, the cardinality of the set of functions $f$ in the dependent product $\prod_{i \in \iota} s(i)$ satisfying $f(i) = a$ for a fixed index $i \in \iota$ and element $a \in s(i)$ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of $s(j)$ for all $j \neq i$ if $a \in s(i)$, and zero otherwise. Formally, $\#{\{f \in \prod_{i \in \iota} s(i) \mid f(i) = a\}} = \begin{cases} \prod_{j \neq i} \#s(j), & a \in s(i) \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$.
